story: My company in Delhi hasn't paid my October 2026 salary of Rs 50,000. I resigned on 31 October 2026.

timeline.user_words: My company in Delhi hasn't paid my October 2026 salary of Rs 50,000.

facts.user_goal: To get my unpaid salary of Rs 50,000 for October 2026.

rules.name: wage_due_date
rules.message: After your last day (31 Oct 2026), the law says final wages must be paid within two working days - about 03 Nov 2026 (not counting Sundays and national holidays; your State can set a different limit).
rules.label: When final pay was due

rules.name: wage_claim_limitation
rules.message: File your wage claim before 03 Nov 2029 (1091 days left). This counts 3 years from 03 Nov 2026 (when October 2026 wages fell due; each later month has its own, later deadline). Don't wait for the last date.
rules.label: Last date to file your wage claim

rules.name: where_to_claim
rules.message: You (or your union) can file a claim before the wage authority. For banks, railways, telecom, mines, insurance and central PSUs this is the Central Government's authority; for other employers it is your State labour department. It can order up to ten times the claim as compensation and recovers unpaid amounts like land revenue. The employer has to prove they paid you.
rules.label: Where to claim

rules.name: amount
rules.message: Unpaid wages: 1 month(s) x Rs 50,000 = Rs 50,000 (before any lawful deductions; HRA and overtime also count as wages for payment).
rules.label: Amount

answer.summary: Your company in Delhi must pay your October 2026 salary of Rs 50,000. Because you resigned, they had to pay you within two working days after 31 October 2026. They did not. You can file a wage claim before the labour authority. You have 3 years from 3 November 2026 to file. The authority can order up to ten times your claim as extra compensation. The employer must prove they paid you.

claims.text: Your company must pay your October 2026 salary of Rs 50,000.
Because you resigned, the company had to pay you within two working days after 31 October 2026.
The employer must prove they paid you.
The labour authority can order up to ten times the unpaid amount as compensation.
You must file your claim within 3 years from 3 November 2026.

next_steps.action: Collect your proof of work and salary. Keep your resignation letter, payslips, and bank statements.
next_steps.why: You need proof to show the authority that you worked and that the salary is unpaid.

next_steps.action: File a wage claim with your Delhi State labour department.
next_steps.why: For a company in Delhi, the State labour department is the correct authority to hear your claim.

next_steps.action: Ask for free legal aid by calling 15100 if you need help filling out the claim form.
next_steps.why: You can get free legal help if your income is below Rs 3,00,000 per year.

support.text: Your company must pay your October 2026 salary of Rs 50,000.
support.reason: The law text does not specify an exact salary amount of Rs 50,000 or mention 'October 2026'. It only establishes general payment timelines for monthly wages (before expiry of seventh day of succeeding month). The sentence adds specific facts (salary amount, month, year) not contained in the law text. However, the legal rule about monthly basis payment before the expiry of the seventh day of the succeeding month is supported. But since the sentence combines specific non-law facts with the rule, and the instruction says to judge only the LEGAL RULE in the sentence and be strict about added conditions, the specific amount and date are not in the law. The core legal rule (monthly basis payment) is supported but the sentence as a whole includes specific facts not in law. Given strict instruction, false.

support.text: Your company must pay your October 2026 salary of Rs 50,000.
support.reason: The law text defines 'wages' but does not mention 'October 2026', 'Rs 50,000', or any specific salary amount or time period. The sentence adds specific facts not contained in the law text. The legal rule about what constitutes wages is supported, but the specific application with amounts and dates is not in the law.

support.text: Because you resigned, the company had to pay you within two working days after 31 October 2026.
support.reason: The law text in section 17(2) explicitly states that where an employee has resigned from service, 'the wages payable to him shall be paid within two working days of his removal, dismissal, retrenchment or, as the case may be, his resignation.' The sentence correctly applies this rule to the resignation scenario with the specific date '31 October 2026' (which is an application to personal facts, which is allowed).

support.text: The employer must prove they paid you.
support.reason: The law text in section 59 explicitly states: 'the burden to prove that the said dues have been paid shall be on the employer.' The sentence correctly states this legal rule.

support.text: The labour authority can order up to ten times the unpaid amount as compensation.
support.reason: The law text in section 45(2) explicitly states that the authority 'may order... the payment of compensation in addition to the claim determined, which may extend to ten times of the claim determined.' The sentence correctly states this legal rule.

support.text: You must file your claim within 3 years from 3 November 2026.
support.reason: The law text in section 45(6) states: 'The application under sub-section (4) may be filed within a period of three years from the date on which claims referred to in sub-section (1) arises.' The sentence specifies '3 November 2026' which is not in the law text. The legal rule (3 years from when claims arise) is supported, but the specific date '3 November 2026' is not in the law text. However, the instruction says the sentence may APPLY the law to the person's own facts (their names, months, amounts, or a date computed from the rule) - that is fine. But '3 November 2026' is a specific date not computed from any rule in the law text. The law text does not provide a basis for this specific date. Therefore false.

support.text: You must file your claim within 3 years from 3 November 2026.
support.reason: The law text in LIM1963_art7 states: 'Three years When the wages accrue due'. The sentence specifies '3 November 2026' which is not in the law text. draft_notes:
How to send it:
1. Find their correct address in your offer letter, salary slip, or the company's registered office on the MCA website (mca.gov.in).
2. Fill every [FILL] slot. Remove anything that isn't true - only state facts you can prove.
3. Send by Speed Post and keep the receipt and the tracking proof of delivery. Also send a copy by email or WhatsApp and keep a screenshot.
4. Wait 15 days. Sending this letter does NOT stop any legal time limit - file your claim/complaint before the deadline shown, even if they haven't replied.
5. Free help to check the letter: legal aid 15100 or Tele-Law 14454.

Laws this letter relies on: Code on Wages, 2019, s.17(1)-(4) (Time limit for payment of wages); Code on Wages, 2019, s.45(1)-(6) (Claims authority, compensation, recovery and time limit); Code on Wages, 2019, s.59 (Burden of proof on employer); Code on Wages, 2019, s.2(d) (Central or State Government: whose authority applies); Code on Wages, 2019, s.2(y) (main part, clauses (a)-(j)) (What counts as "wages")
